who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), port lane for crates/base-db onto blaze-memo, port-1113
where: crates/base-db/src/lib.rs (set_all_crates_with_durability, add_crates, set_primary_crates, set_process_env, crate_durability); crates/base-db/src/input.rs (Crate::create, create_added, give); callers in blaze-lower (const_macros.rs, doctests.rs, lib.rs), blaze-items/src/tests/hashes.rs, blaze-diagnostics/src/tests/lints/names/imports.rs, hir-ty-pure/src/tests/fixture.rs
what: Under blaze-query every input was a free function or method taking &mut Db, so crates above base-db wrote inputs directly, each with its own durability. Moving base-db to a world plus snapshot (writes go through Db::edit and land at commit) changes the signature of every one of those writes, in files of six other crates the lane may not edit.
cost: a port of base-db cannot compile the crates above it on its own; each caller is a hand-off to another lane, listed in the report
cause: the database's write side had no single type: any function with &mut Db could write any input, so the write API was the whole crate's surface rather than one
class: a mutation API spread as free functions over a shared handle, so changing how writes land touches every writer
prevention: every write goes through one type (base_db::Edit, borrowed from Db::edit, consumed by commit), and nothing else takes &mut Db; a clippy disallowed-methods ban on new &mut Db free functions in base-db keeps it so
workaround: listed each caller with the Edit method that replaces it (Edit::create_crate, add_crates, set_all_crates, set_primary_crates, set_process_env, give)
fix: base-db side done in this port (Edit); the callers are ported by their crates' lanes
